artifacts.summary: Confirms the quoted-entry-disables-own-glob root cause at both is_contained_v10 (git-commit-scoped.sh) and its ported twin is_contained (git-commit-phase.sh); supplies a validated minimal fix (parameter-expansion /** suffix-strip plus prefix test) for both sites, a 9-case validation table, confirmation that task 425 is an independent, non-overlapping fix (no dependency edge needed), and test-coverage recommendations modeled on each suite's existing harness.

memory_candidates.content: Bash case-pattern quoting pitfall: `case "$path" in "$entry"/*) ;; esac` fully quotes $entry, which disables glob interpretation of any wildcard characters the VALUE of $entry itself contains (not just the surrounding pattern syntax). If $entry's value is meant to carry a glob suffix like a trailing `/**` (as in file_scope deep-prefix declarations), this idiom silently never matches real paths -- it only matches a path containing the literal asterisk characters. Fix: detect the intended glob suffix via parameter-expansion with escaped asterisks (`${var%/\*\*}` strips a literal two-char `/**` suffix, not a wildcard), then handle that case as an explicit separate branch with a quoted literal base -- never rely on quoting-disabled interpolation of stored/arbitrary string data as a live glob.

In this repo's agent-system, a task's declared file_scope is matched by git-commit-scoped.sh/git-commit-phase.sh as literal strings only, with one sanctioned glob form: a trailing `/**` meaning deep-prefix containment. Shell brace expansion or other glob syntax embedded in a file_scope entry (e.g. `{a,b,c}/**`) is never evaluated -- it matches only as the single literal string it is. This is deliberate (evaluating arbitrary task-authored strings as live shell expansion would be a correctness/safety hazard), not an oversight, so a future file_scope entry relying on brace expansion will silently never match any real path.
